title: Congenital Nephrotic Syndrome: Finnish Type, Denys-Drash and Early Management
subject: ss-paediatric-nephrology
module: Glomerular Diseases, Nephrotic Syndrome and Nephritis

steps.say: Congenital nephrotic syndrome manifests in early infancy with profound proteinuria requiring strict diagnostic chronology.
steps.tx: Apply the chronological **Timing definition of congenital and infantile NS** to guide initial clinical evaluation. Congenital nephrotic syndrome formally presents within the first 3 months of life or 0-90 days from delivery, whereas infantile nephrotic syndrome presents between 3 and 12 months of life, distinguishing neonatal developmental defect categories from acquired post-neonatal glomerulopathies.

left.title: Congenital NS (CNS)
points: Presents within first 3 months of life (0-90 days)
Intrauterine onset typical with fetal proteinuria
Severe genetic podocytopathy or antenatal infection

right.title: Infantile NS (INS)
points: Presents between 3 and 12 months of life

steps.say: Finnish type congenital nephrotic syndrome features severe intrauterine podocyte dysfunction linked to nephrin mutations.
steps.tx: Recognize the genetic and antenatal features of **Finnish type CNS (CNF) NPHS1 genetics** on maternal evaluation. Finnish type CNS is an autosomal recessive mutation in NPHS1 on chromosome 19q13.1 encoding nephrin, presenting with massive intrauterine proteinuria, elevated maternal alpha-fetoprotein (AFP > 10 MoM), and an enlarged placenta exceeding 25% infant birth weight.

steps.say: Podocin defects present across a broad pediatric age spectrum and fail steroid therapy.
steps.tx: Evaluate podocyte structural integrity by testing for **NPHS2 podocin mutations and age of onset** across pediatric presentations. Autosomal recessive mutations in NPHS2 on chromosome 1q25-q31 encode the slit-diaphragm scaffold protein podocin, causing resistant podocytopathy presenting from early infancy up to adolescence, characterized by universal non-responsiveness to corticosteroid immunosuppression.

steps.say: Denys-Drash syndrome links early nephropathy with gonadal dysgenesis and oncologic danger.
steps.tx: Screen for systemic complications defining the **Denys-Drash syndrome triad and WT1 mutations** in infants with early proteinuria. Denys-Drash syndrome is caused by heterozygous missense mutations in WT1 on chromosome 11p13 within exon 8 or 9, featuring a triad of early-onset diffuse mesangial sclerosis (DMS), 46,XY disorder of sex development, and > 90% risk of Wilms tumor.

vis.title: Denys-Drash Syndrome Triad Components
rows: Early rapid progression to end-stage kidney failure

steps.say: Frasier syndrome presents later in life with distinct splice site disruption in the same regulatory gene.
steps.tx: Differentiate atypical gonadal and glomerular phenotypes by detecting **Frasier syndrome WT1 donor splice site** alterations. Frasier syndrome results from WT1 intron 9 splice-site mutations altering the +KTS/-KTS transcription ratio, presenting with progressive adolescent FSGS, complete 46,XY female sex reversal, streak gonads, and high risk of gonadoblastoma rather than Wilms nephroblastoma.

right.title: Frasier Syndrome
points: WT1 intron 9 donor splice site mutation
Risk of gonadoblastoma in streak gonads

steps.say: Supportive protocols sustain infants through continuous replacement and vascular control.
steps.tx: Administer an intensive medical **Aggressive supportive therapy protocol** to stabilize severe neonatal protein excretion. Finnish CNS requires daily intravenous 20% albumin infusions at 3-4 g/kg/day combined with furosemide, oral enalapril and indomethacin to reduce glomerular filtration pressure and urinary protein wasting, along with levothyroxine supplementation to correct severe urinary thyroglobulin losses.

steps.say: Definitive surgical therapy prepares the developing infant for formal allograft placement.
steps.tx: Coordinate specialized surgical milestones governed by **Unilateral vs bilateral nephrectomy timing** in failing infants. Bilateral nephrectomy with initiation of peritoneal dialysis is performed once the infant reaches 7-9 kg weight to halt life-threatening protein loss, severe hypogammaglobulinemia, and recurrent anasarca, thereby optimizing somatic nutrition and growth for definitive kidney transplantation at 10-12 kg body weight.

steps.say: Secondary infectious etiologies must be distinguished because eradication produces complete nephrotic recovery.
steps.tx: Exclude treatable secondary causes by investigating potential **Infectious CNS etiologies** at diagnosis. Congenital nephrotic syndrome can arise from intrauterine infections including congenital syphilis, cytomegalovirus (CMV), toxoplasmosis, and congenital rubella, where early antimicrobial eradication with penicillin G or ganciclovir resolves immune-complex deposition and reverses nephrotic proteinuria without nephrectomy.
